podcast.body: Released in August 1983 on the Rat Cage label, this four-song EP's title track originated from a prank phone call made to a local Carvel Ice Cream store, incorporating samples from Steve Martin's comedy album "A Wild and Crazy Guy" over beats. It was a distinctive departure from the New York Hardcore scene and gained college radio airplay. The song also became the subject of a lawsuit against British Airways for unauthorized sampling, which the Beastie Boys won, earning them their first significant money from music. "The Beastie Boys with Cookie-puss, another release on The Ratchet Cage label, this time from August 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This four-song EP's title track, released in August 1983 on Rat Cage, gained significant college radio airplay and inadvertently made the band "serious money." The concept involved a prank phone call to a local Carvel ice cream store (Carvel sold an ice cream cake called a Cookie Puss), which was then taped and combined with bits from Steve Martin's comedy album *A Wild and Crazy Guy* over some beats. British Airways allegedly used a sample from the song in a commercial without permission, leading to a successful lawsuit where the Beastie Boys won $40,000, which they used to rent an apartment and rehearsal space at 99 Christie Street. "The concept was really simple. First of all, they made a prank phone call to a local Carval ice cream store."
